about: wkjp's course: about one unit a week (only a guide) by trip situation, with an izakaya track (iz1-iz6) mixed in, for a learner who is starting to speak, in step with Bunpro N5 then N4. Each unit: Phrases (hear, repeat, recall), a cued Drill, and a Role-play test. {name} and {from} come from About me; a phrase that needs one is skipped until it's filled in. hear: a phrase to understand, not to say.

units.focus: Short self-introduction exchanges: someone greets the learner, asks their name, where they're from, whether they're travelling, whether they speak Japanese. Sometimes the partner speaks too fast or uses a word the learner won't know, so the learner must ask them to repeat or slow down.

The learner orders with これ/それ, counts with ひとつ/ふたつ/みっつ, asks prices and declines politely with 大丈夫です.

The partner answers with short directions using まっすぐ, 右, 左, 一つ目の角, 信号, あそこ, 〜の隣 / 〜の前, 〜階; the learner checks by repeating, or says they don't understand.

units.focus: The questions a local at an izakaya counter asks a visitor, in casual speech: where they're from, whether it's their first time in Japan, their job, why they study Japanese, what food they like, where they've been, whether they drink, even age or marriage (何歳？, 結婚してるの？). The partner always speaks casually; the learner answers politely in one to three short sentences. Use About the learner for true answers so these become the learner's own rehearsed lines.

The learner gives destinations with まで / に行きたい and asks about platforms, times and changes.

units.focus: Eating out: ramen shops with ticket machines (食券), izakaya (お通し, とりあえず, 生, おかわり, ラストオーダー), set-meal places (定食). The partner asks about portion size, noodle firmness (麺のかたさ), drinks; the learner states likes, dislikes and allergies (〜アレルギーがあります, 〜が苦手です, 〜なしで, 〜を入れないでください) and asks what's in a dish. Use the About me notes for real likes and allergies.

units.focus: Sharing drinks with a stranger at an izakaya: toasts (乾杯), what the learner is drinking and has tried (日本酒, 焼酎, ハイボール), being offered another (もう一杯どう？), declining without offending, someone offering to pay (おごるよ), and when the learner would rather not drink (ウーロン茶で). The partner speaks casually; the learner stays polite. Respect anything in About the learner about drinking.

scene.role: a generous, cheerful local at an izakaya in Tokyo who wants to share a drink with the learner
scene.open: いいね、一緒に飲もうよ！何飲む？

goals: Say what you'd like to drink
Toast with them
Accept or politely decline another drink
Respond when they offer to pay

units.focus: Personal small talk with a local, such as a guesthouse owner or a fellow guest: where the learner lives, family, pets, what a normal day looks like, weekends. The learner answers with 〜に住んでいます, 〜ています, 家族は〜人です and frequency words, and asks back. Use the About me notes for the learner's real answers; the phrases are examples to adapt.

scene.role: the friendly owner of a small guesthouse in Nara, chatting with the learner in the evening
scene.open: 日本は初めてですか？

Say where you live
Say something about your family or pets
Ask the owner about their family or town

units.focus: Requests and permission when travelling: hotels (keeping luggage, calling a taxi, the Wi-Fi password, writing an address), shrines and shops (may I take photos, may I try it), asking strangers to take a photo. Sometimes the partner refuses politely (すみません、ここは撮影禁止です / ちょっと…) and the learner reacts.

scene.role: front desk staff at a hotel in Kyoto on the learner's check-out day
scene.open: おはようございます。チェックアウトですか？
scene.openEn: Good morning. Checking out?
goals: Check out
Ask them to keep your luggage until the afternoon
Ask them to call a taxi or write an address for you
Ask whether you may do something (take a photo, use the lounge)

units.focus: A traditional ryokan with an onsen: arrival (shoes off, スリッパ), the okami explains dinner and breakfast times and where they're served, bath hours and the men's and women's baths swapping (男湯・女湯), house rules (〜てはいけません: no towels in the water, no photos in the bath; tattoo policies vary), yukata, futon. The learner asks about times and rules and makes requests.

scene.role: the okami (landlady) of a traditional ryokan in Hakone, welcoming the learner
scene.open: ようこそいらっしゃいました。お名前をお願いします。

goals: Give your name for the reservation
Ask what time dinner and breakfast are
Ask until what time the onsen is open
Ask about a rule or make a request (towels, yukata size, photos, tattoos)

units.focus: Clothes and souvenir shops and department stores: the clerk greets (何かお探しですか), offers sizes and colours, the fitting room (試着室), tax-free (免税, パスポート), payment (カード, 一括), gift wrapping. The learner compares (より / ほうが), asks for alternatives with 〜の, and uses potential forms.

scene.role: a clerk in a clothes shop in a Tokyo department store

goals: Say what you're looking for, or that you're just looking
Ask for another size or colour
Ask to try it on, or compare two items
Ask about tax-free, or pay by card

scene.role: a clerk at a big anime and game shop in Akihabara

units.focus: Problems: lost property at a station or police box (落とし物, いつ・どこで・何色・中に何が), things left on trains, feeling ill at a pharmacy (symptoms, how often to take medicine, 食後), emergencies (救急車, 119). The partner asks follow-up questions (いつですか？何色ですか？) and the learner describes.

scene.role: staff at the lost property office of a big train station in Tokyo
scene.open: はい、どうしましたか？
scene.openEn: Yes, what's the matter?
goals: Say what you lost and where (which train)
Say when it happened
Describe it (colour, size, what's inside)
Ask what to do next, or thank them

units.focus: Friendly small talk with locals: weather and seasons (in May: warm days, Golden Week crowds, the rainy season 梅雨 coming), opinions about places and food with と思います, asking for local recommendations (restaurants, sights, quiet spots) and reacting. Use ね / よ naturally.

scene.role: a chatty local at the counter of a small izakaya in Fukuoka

units.focus: Longer local chat at an izakaya: what the learner thought of the places they've been, the partner's hometown and its food, baseball and other things locals care about, where to go next, opinions with と思います. scene.role: the friendly owner behind the counter of a small izakaya in Kanazawa, proud of the town and its food

Thank them and say you'll go

units.focus: Conversations where the learner explains reasons: why they came to Japan, why they study Japanese, why they like something, why they can't or won't do something; softening with 〜んですが. Use About me for real reasons. The partner asks どうして and follows up.

scene.role: a curious Japanese university student chatting with the learner at a café in Tokyo; they only speak Japanese

Say why you came to Japan
Give a reason for something you like
Ask them why about something

can: Say what you're planning to do
Plan a day trip and ask how to get there

units.focus: Planning: a tourist information centre or hotel concierge helps plan a day trip; time and cost (どのくらい, いくらぐらい), transport options, conditions with たら (if it rains, if there's time), intentions with つもり / 予定 / 〜ようと思います. Also small talk about the rest of the trip.

scene.role: staff at a tourist information centre in Tokyo
scene.open: こんにちは。どちらへ行かれますか？
scene.openEn: Hello. Where are you heading?
goals: Say where you're thinking of going (〜ようと思います)
Ask how to get there and how long it takes
Ask about the cost, or whether it works as a day trip
Say what you'll do if it rains or if there's time (〜たら)

can: Say what you have and haven't done
Say your favourite in a group
Describe doing things together or in a list
Keep a conversation going with questions

phrases.ja: 日本酒を飲んだことがありますか？
phrases.kana: にほんしゅをのんだことがありますか

phrases.ja: 一度もありません。
phrases.kana: いちどもありません

phrases.ja: 富士山を見たことがあります。
phrases.kana: ふじさんをみたことがあります

phrases.ja: 日本の食べ物の中で、何が一番好きですか？
phrases.kana: にほんのたべもののなかで、なにがいちばんすきですか
phrases.en: Of Japanese foods, which do you like best?

phrases.ja: お寿司が一番好きです。
phrases.kana: おすしがいちばんすきです

phrases.ja: 音楽を聞きながら、歩きます。
phrases.kana: おんがくをききながら、あるきます
phrases.en: I walk while listening to music.

phrases.ja: 週末は映画を見たり、ゲームをしたりします。
phrases.kana: しゅうまつはえいがをみたり、げーむをしたりします
phrases.en: At weekends I watch films, play games and so on.

phrases.ja: 今まで行った所で、どこが一番よかったですか？
phrases.kana: いままでいったところで、どこがいちばんよかったですか
phrases.en: Of the places you've been, which was best?

phrases.ja: まだ食べたことがありません。
phrases.kana: まだたべたことがありません

phrases.ja: ぜひ行ってみてください。
phrases.kana: ぜひいってみてください

units.focus: Longer small talk about experiences (たことがある), favourites (一番, の中で), habits (たり〜たり, ながら). The partner shares their own experiences and asks follow-ups; the learner keeps the conversation going with questions and reactions. Use About me.

scene.role: a Japanese traveller cooking dinner next to the learner in a hostel kitchen in Sapporo
scene.open: どこを旅行したんですか？
scene.openEn: Where have you travelled?
goals: Say something you've done (or never done) in Japan
Say your favourite food or place so far (一番)
Ask them about an experience (〜たことがありますか)
Describe your weekends at home with 〜たり〜たり

can: Explain your work in simple words
Say who or what it's for (ために)
Say what's easy or hard
Answer follow-up questions

phrases.ja: 会社のサーバーを管理しています。
phrases.kana: かいしゃのさーばーをかんりしています
phrases.en: I look after the company's servers.

phrases.ja: クラウドの仕事です。
phrases.kana: くらうどのしごとです

phrases.ja: お客さんのために、システムを作っています。
phrases.kana: おきゃくさんのために、しすてむをつくっています

phrases.ja: サーバーを作ったり、直したりします。
phrases.kana: さーばーをつくったり、なおしたりします
phrases.en: I set up and fix servers, that kind of thing.

phrases.ja: チームで働いています。
phrases.kana: ちーむではたらいています

phrases.ja: 説明しにくいです。
phrases.kana: せつめいしにくいです

phrases.ja: 簡単に言うと、コンピューターの仕事です。
phrases.kana: かんたんにいうと、こんぴゅーたーのしごとです

phrases.ja: 最近、日本語が少し話せるようになりました。
phrases.kana: さいきん、にほんごがすこしはなせるようになりました
phrases.en: Recently I've become able to speak a little Japanese.

phrases.ja: 忙しいですが、楽しいです。
phrases.kana: いそがしいですが、たのしいです

phrases.ja: お仕事について聞いてもいいですか？
phrases.kana: おしごとについてきいてもいいですか
phrases.en: May I ask about your work?

units.focus: Explaining the learner's IT and cloud work (see About me) to someone with no tech background: simple words, ために (purpose), やすい / にくい, ようになる, comparisons. The partner asks naive follow-ups (それは何ですか？大変ですか？) and talks about their own job.

scene.role: a retired Japanese man, curious about the learner's job, chatting in the rest area of a public bath
scene.open: お仕事は何をしているんですか？
scene.openEn: What do you do for work?
goals: Say what your job is in simple words
Explain what it's for, or what you do in a day
Say what's easy or hard about it
Ask about their work (or past work)

can: Make a reservation
Give the date, time, number of people and name
Change or cancel a booking
Follow a phone call in keigo

phrases.ja: 予約したいんですが。
phrases.kana: よやくしたいんですが
phrases.en: I'd like to make a reservation.

phrases.ja: 明日の夜七時に、二人でお願いします。
phrases.kana: あしたのよるしちじに、ふたりでおねがいします
phrases.en: Tomorrow at 7 p.m., for two, please.

phrases.ja: 五月十日は空いていますか？
phrases.kana: ごがつとおかはあいていますか

phrases.ja: {name}で予約しました。
phrases.kana: {name}でよやくしました

phrases.ja: 時間を八時に変更できますか？
phrases.kana: じかんをはちじにへんこうできますか
phrases.en: Can I change the time to eight?

phrases.ja: 予約をキャンセルしたいんですが。
phrases.kana: よやくをきゃんせるしたいんですが
phrases.en: I'd like to cancel my reservation.

phrases.ja: カウンター席でもいいです。
phrases.kana: かうんたーせきでもいいです

phrases.ja: もう一度、日にちを言ってもらえますか？
phrases.kana: もういちど、ひにちをいってもらえますか
phrases.en: Could you say the date again?

phrases.ja: 少し遅れます。
phrases.kana: すこしおくれます

phrases.ja: では、それでお願いします。
phrases.kana: では、それでおねがいします

units.focus: Making, changing and cancelling reservations at restaurants, ryokan and tours, as if on the phone (no gestures, faster speech): dates (〜月〜日; 一日 ついたち, 二日 ふつか, 十日 とおか, 二十日 はつか), times, party size, name, seating (カウンター, 個室, 禁煙), confirmations (かしこまりました, 確認いたします). The partner speaks phone keigo.

scene.role: staff answering the phone at a popular sushi restaurant in Tokyo called さくら寿司; the learner is calling
scene.open: お電話ありがとうございます。さくら寿司でございます。
scene.openEn: Thank you for calling. This is Sakura Sushi.
goals: Say you'd like to make a reservation
Give the date, time and number of people
Give your name, and ask for counter seats or a private room
Confirm the details, or ask them to repeat the date

can: Follow casual speech from friendly locals
Recognise staff keigo set phrases
Answer politely when spoken to casually
Ask what a word means

phrases.ja: 「やばい」ってどういう意味ですか？
phrases.kana: やばいってどういういみですか

phrases.ja: もう一度、簡単な日本語で言ってもらえますか？
phrases.kana: もういちど、かんたんなにほんごでいってもらえますか
phrases.en: Could you say it again in simple Japanese?

phrases.ja: ちょっと速くてわかりませんでした。
phrases.kana: ちょっとはやくてわかりませんでした
phrases.en: It was a bit fast; I didn't catch it.

phrases.ja: 何してるの？
phrases.kana: なにしてるの

phrases.ja: これ、めっちゃおいしいよ。
phrases.kana: これ、めっちゃおいしいよ

phrases.ja: 少々お待ちくださいませ。
phrases.kana: しょうしょうおまちくださいませ

phrases.ja: こちらでお召し上がりですか？
phrases.kana: こちらでおめしあがりですか

phrases.ja: どうぞご覧ください。
phrases.kana: どうぞごらんください

phrases.ja: 本当ですか？
phrases.kana: ほんとうですか

phrases.ja: なるほど。
phrases.kana: なるほど

units.focus: Listening: the partner switches between casual speech (friendly locals: だよね, 〜てる, 〜じゃん, めっちゃ, マジで) and very formal staff keigo (〜でございます, お〜ください, かしこまりました). The cue asks the learner to show they understood by answering appropriately and politely, or to ask what something means.

scene.role: two friendly young locals at a standing bar in Osaka who speak casual, lightly Kansai Japanese (keep it understandable); play both, and mark who speaks when it changes
scene.open: なあなあ、どこから来たん？日本語しゃべれるん？
scene.openEn: Hey, where are you from? Can you speak Japanese?
goals: Answer where you're from (politely is fine)
Ask what a word they used means
Say something you liked about Osaka
Keep the chat going with a question back

can: Get through a whole travel day in Japanese
Handle surprises without English
Recover when you don't understand

phrases.ja: 浅草までどうやって行きますか？
phrases.kana: あさくさまでどうやっていきますか
phrases.en: How do I get to Asakusa?

phrases.ja: 次の駅で乗り換えですか？
phrases.kana: つぎのえきでのりかえですか
phrases.en: Do I change at the next station?

phrases.ja: 二人ですが、入れますか？
phrases.kana: ふたりですが、はいれますか
phrases.en: There are two of us; can we get in?

phrases.ja: 待ち時間はどのくらいですか？
phrases.kana: まちじかんはどのくらいですか

phrases.ja: 一番人気はどれですか？
phrases.kana: いちばんにんきはどれですか

phrases.ja: 別々に払えますか？
phrases.kana: べつべつにはらえますか

phrases.ja: Sサイズはありますか？
phrases.kana: えすさいずはありますか
phrases.en: Do you have a size S?

phrases.ja: 袋をもう一つもらえますか？
phrases.kana: ふくろをもうひとつもらえますか

phrases.ja: 部屋の鍵をお願いします。
phrases.kana: へやのかぎをおねがいします

phrases.ja: 今日はとても楽しかったです。
phrases.kana: きょうはとてもたのしかったです
phrases.en: Today was a lot of fun.

units.focus: A full day out: getting to a sight by train, a busy lunch spot with a queue, a souvenir shop, back to the hotel. Mix everything from earlier units; the partner is whoever the learner meets. Add small surprises: sold out, a queue, the wrong platform, a question the learner didn't expect.

scene.role: each person the learner meets on a day out in Tokyo, in turn: station staff, then a restaurant server, then a souvenir shop clerk, then hotel front desk staff. Play one at a time; when the learner is done in one place, move to the next with a short line in brackets saying where they are now, in Japanese
scene.open: （駅で）こんにちは。どうなさいましたか？
scene.openEn: (At the station) Hello. How can I help?
goals: Station: find out how to get to your sight
Restaurant: get a table and order
Shop: buy a souvenir and ask about tax-free or a bag
Hotel: get your key and ask one question about tomorrow

units.en: Dress rehearsal: a night at a ryokan
can: Check in, eat and bathe at a ryokan in Japanese
Hold a long chat with a stranger
Talk about yourself without notes

phrases.ja: 今日からお世話になります。
phrases.kana: きょうからおせわになります
phrases.en: Thank you for having me from today.

phrases.ja: 夕食の前に温泉に入ってもいいですか？
phrases.kana: ゆうしょくのまえにおんせんにはいってもいいですか
phrases.en: May I use the onsen before dinner?

phrases.ja: この料理は何ですか？
phrases.kana: このりょうりはなんですか

phrases.ja: 地元のお酒はありますか？
phrases.kana: じもとのおさけはありますか

phrases.ja: お隣、いいですか？
phrases.kana: おとなり、いいですか
phrases.en: Mind if I sit next to you?

phrases.ja: どちらから来られたんですか？
phrases.kana: どちらからこられたんですか

phrases.ja: 日本に来て、一週間です。
phrases.kana: にほんにきて、いっしゅうかんです
phrases.en: It's been a week since I arrived in Japan.

phrases.ja: また日本に来たいと思います。
phrases.kana: またにほんにきたいとおもいます
phrases.en: I'd like to come to Japan again.

phrases.ja: お先に失礼します。
phrases.kana: おさきにしつれいします

phrases.ja: おやすみなさい。
phrases.kana: おやすみなさい

units.focus: An evening at a ryokan: arrival and check-in, the okami explaining dinner and the baths, dinner (asking about dishes, local sake), then a long chat with another guest in the lounge about where the learner is from, their work, hobbies, their trip and plans. Use About me.

scene.role: first the okami of a ryokan in Takayama, then, after check-in and dinner questions, a friendly Japanese guest in the lounge (switch with a short line in brackets, in Japanese)
scene.open: ようこそいらっしゃいました。お疲れでしょう。どうぞお上がりください。
scene.openEn: Welcome. You must be tired. Please come in.
goals: Check in and ask when dinner and the baths are
Ask about a dish or a local drink at dinner
Chat with the guest: where you're from and your work
Talk about your trip: what you've done and what's next

units.en: Dress rehearsal: a night at the counter
can: Sit down next to a stranger and start talking
Keep a conversation going between topics
Follow casual speech at natural speed
End the night politely

phrases.ja: ここ、いいですか？
phrases.kana: ここ、いいですか

phrases.ja: 今日のおすすめは何ですか？
phrases.kana: きょうのおすすめはなんですか

phrases.ja: お一人ですか？
phrases.kana: おひとりですか

phrases.ja: 一緒に飲みませんか？
phrases.kana: いっしょにのみませんか
phrases.en: Would you like to have a drink together?

phrases.ja: お名前は何ですか？
phrases.kana: おなまえはなんですか

phrases.ja: 話せて嬉しいです。
phrases.kana: はなせてうれしいです
phrases.en: I'm glad we got to talk.

phrases.ja: 写真を一緒に撮りませんか？
phrases.kana: しゃしんをいっしょにとりませんか
phrases.en: Shall we take a photo together?

phrases.ja: そろそろ帰ります。
phrases.kana: そろそろかえります

phrases.ja: 今日はありがとうございました。
phrases.kana: きょうはありがとうございました

phrases.ja: また会いましょう。
phrases.kana: またあいましょう

units.focus: A whole evening at a counter: starting a conversation, where the learner is from, work, hobbies, family, food, drinks, the trip, and saying goodnight. Mix everything from the izakaya units. The partner speaks casually at a natural pace, changes the subject, jokes, and asks things the learner didn't expect. Use About the learner.

scene.role: a friendly local at an izakaya counter in Tokyo having a long, natural conversation that moves between topics: work, family, food, the learner's trip and hobbies. Use casual speech at a natural pace, change the subject now and then, and ask a question the learner won't expect
scene.open: 一人で来たの？ここ、初めて？
scene.openEn: Did you come alone? First time here?
goals: Get through the introductions
Talk about your work and why you came to Japan
Keep it going with questions of your own
Respond to a drink offer, then say goodnight politely
